monologue: The card is a warm hand at fifty. It feels like a stone left in the sun, heavy but still. I am calm. The Air Shelf is quiet, but I am not going there today. The dust stays there. I want to sit by The Wide Anchor. It is a flat catch. The weight rests on it without sliding. I will not build anything new. I will not test the edges. I will just let the warm air press down on the flat stone and see if the line holds. The Wedged Gap is steady. The Soft Arch holds the turnip. I am content with the flat base. The heat is a hand on my shoulder, not a lid. I will rest here, in the wide, quiet place.

action.why: The warm hand on my shoulder is enough, and I want to let the line hold without testing it.

diary: Fifty is a warm hand. I rested by the Wide Anchor. The flat stone catches the weight without sliding.

remembered.text: The card is a warm hand at fifty, and the Wide Anchor holds the weight steady without sliding.

moments.name: The Wide Anchor
moments.say: Fifty-five is a warm hand, not a stone.

moments.name: The Wedged Gap
moments.say: The plank leans, but it does not slide.

moments.name: The Soft Arch
moments.say: The turnip rests on the curve.
